skill.name: systematic-debugging
skill.description: Guide technical debugging through root-cause investigation, pattern comparison, focused hypothesis testing, minimal fixes, and regression verification.
skill.summary: Find root causes before applying focused, verified fixes.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

content.value_statement: Quick fixes often hide the real cause and create regressions. This skill structures investigation, hypothesis testing, implementation, and verification around collected evidence.
actual_capabilities: Structures debugging into investigation, pattern analysis, hypothesis testing, and implementation phases.
Guides review of errors, reproduction steps, recent changes, and environmental differences.
Traces invalid values backward through callers to identify their original source.
Compares broken behavior with working examples and complete reference implementations.
Tests one root-cause hypothesis using the smallest practical change.
Verifies the selected fix with a failing test and regression checks.
limitations: Requires relevant errors, logs, code, or reproduction details to build reliable hypotheses.
Cannot guarantee a root cause when the failure is intermittent and evidence is unavailable.
Provides a general methodology rather than framework-specific diagnostic automation.
Does not replace specialized profilers, observability systems, or security analysis.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Application Bugs
use_cases.description: Trace unexpected application behavior to its source before changing production code.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Failing Tests
use_cases.description: Separate timing symptoms, polluted state, and invalid setup data through focused experiments.

use_cases.title: Investigate Pipeline Failures
use_cases.description: Instrument component boundaries to locate where data or configuration first becomes incorrect.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Test Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this failing test systematically. Identify missing evidence, state one root-cause hypothesis, and propose the smallest verification step: [failure details]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a reproducible test failure with an error message.

prompt_templates.title: Trace an Invalid Value
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace this invalid value backward through the call chain. Identify its earliest source and distinguish the root cause from downstream symptoms: [trace details]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when incorrect data appears deep in execution.

prompt_templates.title: Isolate a Component Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Design minimal instrumentation for each component boundary. Specify inputs, outputs, configuration checks, and one run that will locate the failing component: [system details]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for services, pipelines, or integrations with several boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Reassess Repeated Fix Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these failed fixes for shared state or coupling. Decide whether another hypothesis is justified or an architectural discussion is required: [attempt history]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after three or more focused fixes have failed.

output_examples.input: A unit test fails because a project directory is empty.
output: Observed symptom: initialization runs in the current directory.
Root-cause hypothesis: setup data is read before initialization.
Verification: inspect the first assignment and reproduce with one focused test.

output_examples.input: A continuous integration job fails between build and signing.
output: Capture the artifact name and checksum after the build.
Capture the received path and configuration before signing.
Compare both boundaries in one failing run.

output_examples.input: Three attempted fixes reveal new shared-state failures.
output_examples.output: Stop applying patches. Document the coupling revealed by each attempt and discuss the architecture before making another change.

best_practices: Collect reproducible evidence before proposing a fix.
Change one variable at a time and record the result.
Add a failing test, fix the source, and check for regressions.
anti_patterns: Do not stack several speculative fixes into one test run.
Do not patch the visible symptom without tracing its input.
Do not continue repeated fixes when evidence indicates architectural coupling.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for bugs, test failures, and unexpected behavior that require evidence-based diagnosis before implementation.

faq.question: Can it debug any programming language?
faq.answer: Yes. The method is language independent, but diagnostics still depend on the available tools and project context.

faq.question: Does it apply fixes automatically?
faq.answer: It guides a focused fix after root-cause investigation. Actual changes depend on the agent, permissions, and user request.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the error, stack trace, reproduction steps, recent changes, expected behavior, and relevant logs.

faq.question: How does it handle flaky tests?
faq.answer: It recommends waiting for observable conditions and isolating the test that first pollutes shared state.

faq.question: What happens after several fixes fail?
faq.answer: After three failed focused fixes, it recommends stopping and discussing possible architectural coupling before continuing.
